title: Safe party food: the Five Keys and the danger zone

say: Safe party food: the Five Keys and the danger zone.
This is the video for module one of Catering Basics and Food Safety: safe catering foundations.
Catering is cooking for people who trust you with their health. It adds three things to good cooking. Scale: you cook five or ten times more than usual.

panel.heading: People trust you with their health
items: Scale: five or ten times more food
Time pressure: hot and safe on time
Safety decided by time and temperature

say: Responsibility: the guests are not your family, and some may be elderly, pregnant, very young or allergic.

panel.heading: People trust you with their health

say: And time pressure: the food must be ready, hot and safe at an exact time.

say: In this video you will learn the rules that keep rice, stew and chicken safe for hours.

say: Key one. Keep clean. Wash hands with soap and clean running water before handling food, and after the toilet, raw meat, money or rubbish. Anyone with diarrhoea, vomiting or an infected cut should not handle food that day.

panel.heading: The Five Keys to Safer Food
items: Use safe water and raw materials

say: Key two. Separate raw and cooked. Use separate boards and knives for raw meat, and store raw meat covered, below cooked food in the fridge.

panel.heading: The Five Keys to Safer Food
items: Use safe water and raw materials

say: Key three. Cook thoroughly. Meat, poultry and eggs must reach 70 degrees Celsius at the centre.

panel.heading: The Five Keys to Safer Food
items: Use safe water and raw materials

say: Key four. Keep food at safe temperatures. We will look at this closely in a moment.

panel.heading: The Five Keys to Safer Food
items: Use safe water and raw materials

say: Key five. Use safe, treated water and good raw materials. Reject swollen or dented cans, mouldy grains and food past its expiry date.

panel.heading: The Five Keys to Safer Food
items: Use safe water and raw materials

say: For example, Funmi caters a naming ceremony for 60 guests. She uses a red board for raw chicken and a green board only for cabbage and carrots, and keeps the coleslaw covered on a separate table.

panel.heading: Stop germs moving to ready food
right: One board for chicken, then salad
Let raw meat drip onto salad
Leave salad out in the heat

say: The common mistake is using the same board for raw chicken and then for coleslaw cabbage, or reusing the marinade bowl for cooked chicken. Coleslaw is not cooked, so nothing kills germs that land on it.

panel.heading: Stop germs moving to ready food
right: One board for chicken, then salad
Let raw meat drip onto salad
Leave salad out in the heat

say: Bacteria grow fastest at warm temperatures, like a Nigerian afternoon. First, cook meat to 70 degrees at the centre.

panel.heading: Keep food out of the danger zone
items: No more than 2 hours at room temperature
Reheat once, steaming hot all through

say: Keep rice, stew and meat steaming hot, above 60 degrees, until served.

panel.heading: Keep food out of the danger zone
items: No more than 2 hours at room temperature
Reheat once, steaming hot all through

say: Keep coleslaw, salad and cream desserts chilled, below 5 degrees.

panel.heading: Keep food out of the danger zone
items: No more than 2 hours at room temperature
Reheat once, steaming hot all through

say: Never leave cooked food at room temperature for more than 2 hours.

panel.heading: Keep food out of the danger zone
items: No more than 2 hours at room temperature
Reheat once, steaming hot all through

say: Reheat only once, until steaming hot all through. The danger zone is between 5 and 60 degrees. Unsafe food can look, smell and taste normal, so decide by time and temperature, never by tasting.

panel.heading: Keep food out of the danger zone
items: No more than 2 hours at room temperature
Reheat once, steaming hot all through
panel.rule: Danger zone: 5°C to 60°C. Do not decide safety by tasting.

say: Cooked rice needs special care. Rice can carry spores that cooking does not kill. If cooked rice sits warm for hours, they make toxins that reheating does not destroy. So, to cool food, spread it into shallow trays, not one deep pot.

panel.heading: Cooling food quickly
items: Stand them in cold water with ice
Label with the dish and the date

say: Stand the containers in a basin of cold water with ice.

say: When steam stops rising, cover and refrigerate, below 5 degrees, well within the 2-hour limit.

panel.heading: Cooling food quickly
items: Stand them in cold water with ice
Label with the dish and the date

say: Label each container with the dish and date. And when in doubt, throw it out.

panel.rule: Never leave cooked rice sitting warm on the counter.

say: Chioma has two insulated coolers and a probe thermometer. She warms each cooler with hot water for 10 minutes first, so the cold walls do not chill the food.

panel.heading: Chioma's holding log
items: Warm the cooler with hot water first

say: At 10:30 am the rice reads 85 degrees and the chicken 78. She fills the coolers hot and closes them at once.

panel.heading: Chioma's holding log
items: Warm the cooler with hot water first

say: At 12:15 pm at the venue, the rice still reads 68 degrees, above 60.

panel.heading: Chioma's holding log
items: Warm the cooler with hot water first

say: At 3:30 pm the leftover rice reads 52, below 60, so she does not take it home for resale. She writes every reading on a log sheet as evidence of safe practice.

panel.heading: Chioma's holding log
items: Warm the cooler with hot water first

say: To remember. Apply the Five Keys to every dish. Keep raw and ready food apart. Cook to 70 degrees, hold above 60 or below 5. Never more than 2 hours at room temperature. And use a probe thermometer and write the readings down.

panel.heading: Remember
items: Five Keys for every dish, not only meat
Separate boards for raw and ready food
Cook to 70°C; hold above 60°C or below 5°C
Never more than 2 hours at room temperature
Use a thermometer and write it down

say: Now practise. Map your kitchen capacity: your pots, burners, helpers and transport. Do a Five Keys audit and fix two gaps this week. And test how long your cooler really keeps food above 60 degrees.
